config.grain_rationale: Each record is one QBCC licence held by a licensee (individual or company). Business attributes of the licence holder (name, ABN, ACN, business address) are mapped onto the entity; licence-specific attributes (number, grade, class, financial category) are not entity fields and are left unmapped.

record_id.rationale: '_id' is the CKAN datastore row id and is 508/508 distinct in the discovery sample; 'Licence Number' had only 506 distinct out of 508 rows (duplicate licence numbers), so it is not unique per record.

fields.rationale: Column is the licensee name; publisher evidence states a licence is issued to an individual or company (legal persons) and the name is the entity as named on the licence. Values are personal/company registered names (e.g. 'JUSTIN WILLIAM PAGE', 'FLASH AIR CONDITIONING AND ELECTRICAL PTY LTD'), so legal_name rather than trading_name.
ABN column of shape '99 999 999 999' with 99.6% checksum validity in profiling; the abn transform strips spaces and validates checksum.
ACN column of shape '999 999 999' with 100% checksum validity in profiling; acn transform strips spaces and validates checksum.

Publisher evidence: the company application collects the licensee's business address and it is published in the register. Values are a combined street/locality/'QLD'/postcode string; no reliable separate locality/postcode columns, so only the full address is mapped.
State abbreviation (e.g. 'QLD') is embedded in the address string; extracted by regex then normalised via the state transform. Sample is a QLD register so nearly all will be QLD.

constants.rationale: Queensland Building and Construction Commission register; all addresses in profiling carry an Australian state (QLD).

unmapped.reason: CKAN internal datastore row id; used only for record_id, not a business identifier.
Identifies the licence, not the business; also not unique per record (506 distinct / 508 rows). Mapping a licence ID as a business identifier would be wrong.

Describes whether the licence is held by an individual or company. Publisher evidence states a licence category does not by itself establish the holder's legal form, so this is ambiguous for entity_type; left unmapped to avoid a wrong enum.
Coded form (I/C) of Licence Type DESC; same ambiguity for entity_type.
Financial category of the licence (e.g. 'Self Certification - Trade'); a licence attribute, not an entity field.
Coded form of the licence financial category; not an entity field.
Grade of the licence (Trade Contractor, Site Supervisor, etc.); a licence attribute, not an entity field.
Class/occupational category of the licence (Carpentry, Plumbing, etc.); a licence attribute, not an entity field.

config.notes: Advertised as CSV but the resource is a CKAN datastore_search JSON response: records live under result.records (record_path), with an outer help/success envelope. Individual licence holders appear as personal names in Licensee Name (legal_name for natural persons is acceptable here since the licensee is the legal person holding the licence; entity_type intentionally left unknown because Licence Type individual/company is a licence category, per publisher evidence). Business addresses are single combined strings with an embedded state; only address.full and address.state mapped, locality/postcode not reliably separable. No date columns present, so no entity.date_registered or observation.valid_* set. One ABN in the sample fails checksum and is correctly rejected by the abn transform.

fields.reason: Licensee Name carries the person/company named on the licence, and the held-out values are personal names or registered-looking company names ('CRAIG MAXWELL NIXON', 'Christopher Angus Fisher'). Publisher evidence confirms a licence is held by an individual or company, so mapping this to legal_name with claim_scope current_legal_name is defensible. Caveat: for individuals the value may be a personal name rather than a registered business name; that is inherent in the source and does not make the target wrong.

ABN is present with the standard 11-digit spacing, the trim/null_if/abn pipeline validates the checksum, and every emitted value in the held-out records ('81559814080', '38725125523', '71430288473', '57622415356', '87886699262') is checksum-consistent. Conditional 'present' guard is appropriate.

ACN column is consistently null in the held-out records, so no observation is emitted; the trim/null_if/acn chain is a correct treatment when a value appears and does not fabricate anything. No wrong emission observed.

Mapped to address.full with claim_scope licence_holder_address. Publisher evidence says the business address is published and is the licensee's business address, so it is the entity's own address and not a licensed premises address — acceptable. However, the values are free-text strings that mix street, locality, state and postcode, and some (e.g. '51,107 Stanworth Rd Boondall QLD 4034') contain ambiguous unit/lot fragments; a full-address claim is reasonable but the lack of any structure makes it only partially verifiable.

State is reliably recoverable from the embedded abbreviation ('... QLD 4510'), every held-out record yields QLD, and the state transform normalises it. No non-Australian address appears in the sample, so no false enum assignment is visible.
Constant AU is supported by all held-out addresses carrying an Australian state and postcode, consistent with a Queensland register. No NZ or foreign address in the sample contradicts it.

missed.reason: Values 'Individual'/'Company' are the register's own statement of whether the licence holder is a natural person or a company. The config leaves this unmapped citing ambiguity, but for the value 'Company' (and 'Individual' paired with an ACN/ABN-to-ACN match) it is strong evidence for entity_type. At minimum a conditional rule company-only would be safe; note a bare 'Individual' does not establish sole_trader.

Coded I/C form of Licence Type DESC; the 'C' code supports entity_type=company with the same conditional logic. Leaving it fully unmapped forfeits the only explicit entity-form evidence in the source.

critic.summary: ABN and state extraction are sound; the address is the holder's own business address, so claim_scope is fine, though full-address claims rest on unstructured strings. The real gap is entity_type: the source's 'Licence Type DESC/CODE' explicitly distinguishes Individual vs Company and should be used (at least conditionally for 'Company') rather than discarded. No incorrect dates, no legacy record-level validity, no licence/contract number misused as a business identifier, and no trading-name-as-legal-name error was observed. Note the grain claim is licence-level while entity fields are holder-level, so repeated holders across licence rows will duplicate entity observations — that is a grain concern, not a per-rule mapping error.

publisher_evidence.notes: A licence may be held by an individual or company. The QBCC licence number identifies the licence. An ABN is issued separately for tax and trading purposes. A licence category does not by itself establish the holder's legal form.
The company application collects ACN, ABN and the licensee's business address. The business address is published in the licence register.
